## Why the previous serializer ideas remain unimplemented

XML item transforms plus `WriteLinesToFile` do not establish arbitrary metadata
escaping and bounded observer-owned string materialization. The proposed helper
therefore does not use generic joins, metadata cloning, a binlog or an environment
dump to serialize SDK items.

The pinned MSBuild RoslynCodeTaskFactory is also unsuitable for the requested
preserved helper image without changing factory/environment behavior. In exact
MSBuild commit `02bf66295b64ab368d12933041f7281aad186a2d`,
`RoslynCodeTaskFactory.cs:763` byte-loads the emitted assembly; lines777–779
delete the DLL before task Execute, and lines682–684 normally delete the C#
source. Changing `MSBUILDLOGCODETASKFACTORYOUTPUT`, replacing the factory, or
reconstructing an assembly from a loaded module is outside this first observer.
That alternative remains unmet/unimplemented, not an overall task blocker.

## Fixed compiler and import mechanism

The finite alternative compiles one fixed C# evidence helper inside the original
single `dotnet build Source/Dafny/Dafny.csproj -c Release -m:1` stage. This is an
additional compiler phase within that build and adds owned compiler/Python
children. It is not another `dotnet build`, MSBuild evaluation, managed logger,
global plugin, SDK evaluation or runtime proof invocation.

The only new outer build argument is the supported extension property
`-p:CustomAfterMicrosoftCommonTargets={ownedRoot}/source/B3AssetsObserver.targets`.
Exact `Microsoft.Common.CurrentVersion.targets:39,6906` provides its default and
conditional Import. Admission must reject a pre-existing user/environment
extension or an existing default Custom.After.Microsoft.Common.targets that this
argument would suppress. The fixed parent project/source/import closure and
captured SDK files must justify the original default absent-file case; if that
closure cannot be established, observation preparation fails rather than assuming
an empty prior evaluated property. No second SDK call is permitted to resolve
this gap. The supplied extension argument and this limitation are recorded.

All new task names, targets, properties, item outputs and paths have the prefix
`B3AssetsObserver`. The imported targets read existing SDK properties/items but
never assign, remove or add any SDK/project consumer item or property. An own
owner-eligibility property restricts compilation/capture to the canonical
`Source/Dafny/Dafny.csproj`, `net8.0`, `Release`, `AnyCPU`, non-design-time owner.
Project references retain their ordinary builds and acquire no helper execution.
Exec and UsingTask paths/conditions come from fixed validated own-namespace
values; SDK item paths are not used as commands. Only that eligible owner defines
new dependency targets for the ten capture hooks.

`Microsoft.Common.tasks:106–109` registers the existing fully qualified
`Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.BuildTasks.Csc` task. The proposal uses that registration
rather than defining/overriding Csc. Exact Roslyn commit
`3fb752d448006a3144a60ccf181d745e555422f9` is the SDK8.0.425 compiler toolset
source declared in SDK `eng/Version.Details.xml`; that declaration is provenance,
not a binary/source attestation. The distribution task/compiler/ref/host file
hashes are captured and compared to the identified SDK8.0.425 inventory.

The inert selector contains every compiler parameter and empty/unbound field.
There is one source, `B3AssetsObserver.cs`, and two fixed SDK reference assemblies:
`ref/netstandard.dll` and `ref/Microsoft.Build.Framework.dll`. Output is the fresh
owned `build/B3AssetsObserver.dll`; it is not a Dafny output/reference. The task
implements ITask/ICancelableTask directly, without a Utilities.Core base class,
package resolution, analyzers, generated files, reflection-based item traversal,
subprocesses or SDK calls. The proposed source must still pass later source/API
review and compilation; this English note does not claim those checks ran.

Csc uses explicit Library, C#12, nullable enabled, deterministic, checked, safe,

UseSharedCompilation is false. The current fixed SDK inventory must confirm the

Csc's own CommandLineArgs output goes to a new own item list. The producer
source/explicit options must justify a finite output grammar before any XML
materialization: at most256 rows/65,536 UTF16 units; fixed ordinary ASCII paths,
no CR/LF, quote injection, semicolon item splitting or response-file inputs. A

## Preservation before the first helper load

Ordinary UsingTask registers AssemblyFile while the project is evaluated;
TaskRegistry:317–444 records that path and GetTaskFactory:1369–1394 loads on first
task use through AssemblyTaskFactory:249–279. An eligible capture target depends
on an own prepare target. That target compiles and preserves the helper before
any call to `B3AssetsObserver.CaptureTask`. UsingTask is not conditioned on a
not-yet-existing success marker during project evaluation; the invocation is
conditioned on a fixed own marker established after preparation. This order does
not prove an atomic physical LoadFrom/image binding.

After Csc, a fixed pre-load Python data-capture child runs inside the same build:
resolved current Python, `-I -S -B`, a fixed source path, one fixed mode
`--preserve-before-load`, one own positional ASCII control path and its SHA256. Its source/control bytes,
interpreter and explicit finite import closure are hashed before launch. The
child imports only sys, posix, time and _sha2, with Python3.12/Linux-x64 admitted
explicitly. It does not import json/pathlib/hashlib. Its inert selector freezes
the22 allowed startup/explicit module names and six possible named Python source
origins; built-in/frozen modules bind to the interpreter image. The _sha2 module
must be either a recorded builtin or an exact frozen3.12 x64 extension file, with
no crypto/version/module fallback. Unexpected startup origins fail observation
preparation. It has no user/site/PYTHONPATH imports, cache writes, subprocesses,
network, SDK evaluation, recursive filesystem scan or arbitrary paths. The helper
and bootstrap compilation/source remain private design until full source review.
There is one such child, bounded10seconds within the original1800second stage.

The control has exactly14 ordered ASCII/LF fields: schema marker, source path/hash,
DLL path, two reference path/hash pairs, compiler-argument path, declared-option
seal, preservation root, source seal, immediately captured compiler LastTaskResult
and own compiler ExitCode. The separate raw control SHA binds all
fields. Paths/hashes have fixed admitted grammar; split/decode allocations are
limited to64KiB and14 rows before parsing. Actual compiler arguments are data,
not executed command text. There is no arbitrary JSON parser in this child.

The bootstrap opens only fixed own source/DLL/metadata files and the two fixed
SDK refs, using no-follow regular-file descriptors, length-before-copy limits,
streamed reads, before/after fstat and SHA256. It preserves the FIRST source and
DLL bytes into new immutable artifact paths before the first UsingTask use;
it never overwrites them with later failure observations. It validates exact
fixed options/source/ref/hash identities and publishes a bounded success marker
only on complete capture. If it fails, the marker is absent and captures are
skipped/incomplete. For handled nonfatal bootstrap faults, continuation is requested; preparation,
registration, load, parameter, import or fatal failures may instead abort the build.
The qualifier is then unrun and the new primary build failure is retained. Built-in Copy/GetFileHash are not used on SDK item arrays:
GetFileHash mutates item metadata, and neither builtin establishes this finite
pre-load file contract. Own parameter paths have a fixed ASCII grammar, so Exec
shell text contains no caller-controlled metacharacters or substitutions.

The helper rechecks the preserved first source/DLL/control association before
each frame, records actual Locations/names for exactly the CaptureTask, ITask, Object,
FileStream and SHA256 type-assembly anchors (not a full CLR/native dependency
closure), and compares file hashes after each frame and at final
export. The coordinator preserves SDK distribution task/host/refs and Python
interpreter/import file identities before/after/final. Named module paths are
recorded within a fixed32-file/8MiB identity-reading cap, not scanned recursively.
Python interpreter bytes have their separate existing regular-file bound; module
hash records do not require copying the whole Python installation. The expected
fixed import names (listed now) and actual file identities must be frozen in the source checkpoint
before execution; a new unexpected module/path is observation failure. File pins
and loaded Location evidence do not constitute signed or atomic load attestation.

The compiler task can fail before helper Execute, and CLR/task load can fail too.
Csc/own Exec/task calls request WarnAndContinue/diagnostic receipt behavior for
actual handled nonfatal paths; registration/load/binding/import/fatal faults are
not universally covered. An aborted build is the new primary failure, and earlier
historical failure evidence stays intact; original SDK errors are not suppressed. The
serializer returns success only as an MSBuild continuation signal; its separate
observation status remains failed/incomplete on any fault. New compiler warnings
and unavoidable engine intrinsics such as MSBuildLastTaskResult are reported.
Before source approval, audit the fixed consumed import closure for sensitivity
to these intrinsic task outcomes; do not claim every MSBuild property is unchanged.
There are no observer task output parameters into SDK properties/items.

## Exact ten boundary hooks and source-derived reconstruction limits

The selector freezes before/after hooks for these five source targets:

| Target | Exact SDK source start |
|---|---|
| ResolvePackageAssets | Microsoft.PackageDependencyResolution.targets:230 |
| ResolveTargetingPackAssets | FrameworkReferenceResolution.targets:395 |
| ResolveLockFileCopyLocalFiles | Microsoft.PackageDependencyResolution.targets:516 |
| _HandlePackageFileConflicts | Microsoft.NET.ConflictResolution.targets:25 |
| GenerateBuildDependencyFile | Microsoft.NET.Sdk.targets:248 |

Within each hook, the same fixed65 property expansions,46 individually bound
item arrays and44 GetMetadata names are captured. Their whole ordered lists are
in the selector; no dynamic include, regex, wildcard or name guess adds a field.
All zero-length/null arrays are recorded. Null parameter binding and an empty
array are distinct, without claiming whether an empty SDK item set was defined.
Every row has its source-array ordinal. Duplicates are preserved, even when the
same ItemSpec has different metadata. No sort, Distinct, filename grouping or
metadata dictionary can erase them.

Each metadata getter's returned JSON value is null, empty string or a nonempty
string. Those three cases remain distinct. ITaskItem.GetMetadata alone does not
prove whether metadata was absent, inherited or explicitly empty. Metadata
presence is therefore always `not-observed`. The helper does not enumerate or
clone custom metadata. Property values are task parameter expansion observations,
not evidence of whether the original property was unset, global or locally set.
The fixed whitelist includes target/cache/deps paths, framework/RID/platform/
copy settings, conflict preferred packages, version/assembly and relevant target
conditions. It includes the SDK/compiler/import identity paths for correspondence.

TargetBuilder:421–461 schedules dependencies and before hooks; hooks are not
inserted into task bodies. A before hook is a native target boundary after any
applicable dependencies, not necessarily the first statement's task parameter
state. Target conditions, previous-target caching and Inputs/Outputs incremental
skips can still make the body/task execution unknown. Other registered sibling
hooks may interpose; their pinned definitions/ordering/conditions need later
source reasoning, not an invented direct execution record. Actual own hook
sequence is captured; no global order of the five targets is presumed.

In particular, `_RuntimeAssetsForConflictResolution` is created INSIDE the
conflict target at32–37, after its before hook. The conflict target constructs
its actual task input list and replaces Reference/Analyzer/ReferenceCopyLocalPaths
with duplicate-sensitive filtered lists. The GenerateBuildDependencyFile target
removes conflicts from runtime/native/resource/RID lists at266–271 after its
before hook. These transformations may be reconstructed from exact target source,
ordered boundary data and justified intervening conditions, but the first
observer labels them `source-derived`, not actual task-input/output attestation.

Conflict output cannot certify a winner/rule: exact
ResolvePackageFileConflicts.cs:221–231 constructs a losing SourcePath row with
ConflictItemType/NuGetPackageId, without winner/version/rule metadata. Capture all
that is actually returned, but do not reinterpret it as a full conflict decision.

## Bounds, failure preservation and completeness

The original1800second owned build stage, six original ownership helpers,
32MiB log cap and256MiB whole artifact cap remain authoritative. SDK Csc allocation
and MSBuild task binding already occur before the observer Execute method. The
observer bounds only its own extra copies, holders, serialization and output; it
does not claim to bound original SDK/compiler/metadata-getter allocations.

Each observer frame has at most4096 rows per array,8192 rows total,450,000 metadata
gets,2,097,152 total UTF16 string units and8MiB encoded output. Ordinary returned
strings are at most16,384 UTF16 units; the named import-list string alone is at
most131,072. Ten frames together have at most65,536 rows/28MiB. Fixed row/holder
counts are checked before new holder arrays, and every copied occurrence is
charged. A bounded exact char walk sizes JSON escaping BEFORE observer-owned
encoding/materialization. Printable ASCII is literal except quote/backslash;
controls/non-ASCII use exact escapes; unmatched surrogates fail observation.
Strings are emitted in bounded64KiB buffers. There is no huge concatenated JSON
string. Rechecking the retained input observations detects mutation; it is not
an atomic snapshot theorem for adversarial mutable task objects.

Each Execute has a5second cooperative serialization limit; the whole owned stage
still imposes its original deadline and cancellation/cleanup rules. Observation
bytes total at most64MiB, including frames/tables/raw/helper/bootstrap/failure
receipts and partial files; every output growth is charged before writing. The
existing artifact bound is enforced independently. Reserve observer space before
launch without changing the six helper bodies or loosening logs, stage deadline
or cleanup. If combined output cannot fit, observation is incomplete, not pruned
or silently truncated. Fixed-source/helper/metadata limits are256KiB/512KiB/64KiB;
first helper/ref/bootstrap evidence together is at most8MiB.

Frames use fresh exclusive paths and publish complete files only after bounded
capture and stable before/after association. Partial bytes have distinct prefix
hash/length labels; they cannot satisfy frame-schema/completeness. Failure receipts
are at most32KiB, bounded exception type/message plus immutable known identities,
without stack/environment dumps. Idempotent finally capture cannot mask the
original build/qualifier failure. Any forced child cleanup or residual identity
remains the original owned-stage failure; compiler/Python children do not get a
new ownership exemption or a proof-work label.

Boundary coverage requires all ten unique slots, contiguous sequence0–9, each
before preceding its paired after, one eligible owner, exact field/array/getter
inventory, all rows/ordinals, consistent source/helper/input hashes and preserved
first bytes. Missing, duplicate, conditional/incremental or unknown hooks are
explicit incomplete observations. Ten hooks/five pairs can satisfy boundary coverage
while `targetBodyExecution:not-observed` and `taskParametersObserved:false` remain
true. No field named exclusionQualified/runtimeQualified/CLRSelected can become
true in this observer. Existing qualifier/runtime acceptance is reported separately.

command grammar, preserve-before-load ordering, extra children/intrinsic outcomes,
ITaskItem read-only API use, all bounds-before-allocation paths, fixed source/data

Meaningful later observer controls need distinguish: ordered duplicate ItemSpecs
with differing metadata; null/empty/nonempty returns; escape/control/Unicode round
trip; malformed surrogate; before/at/above row/string/byte/aggregate limits;
metadata mutation during capture; missing/duplicate/reversed hooks; changed source,

compiler failure and partial DLL; preserved first bytes versus later failure;
conditional/incremental body-not-observed; conflict loser without invented winner;
no SDK item mutation; intentional helper child failure versus original natural
owned-stage completion. These are prospective names/categories only, not newly
implemented or executed assertions/denominators. All actual original23 qualifier

A second separately reviewed phase may reason about full raw-candidate disposition
using these observations and exact source transforms. This first proposal does
not admit Registry, waive a missing DLL, substitute framework bytes or claim CLR
loading. Unknown disposition continues to fail the original qualifier.

## Revision 2 continuation qualification

WarnAndContinue does not cover every task preparation failure. Exact pinned
TaskBuilder's InitializeForBatch failure throws an InvalidProjectFile error before
ExecuteInstantiatedTask's nonfatal ContinueOnError handling. New malformed imports,
registration/load/parameter initialization and fatal observer/compiler preparation
can abort the original build. In that case report its actual new primary build
failure and qualifier/corpus as unrun; retain5502 and the earlier unidentified a9cf
failed receipts. No old assertion is skipped/admitted to manufacture a passing
qualifier. Only actually handled nonfatal returns/faults may continue. The future
source must preserve the distinction between primary stage failure and secondary
observation/preservation faults, including partial compiler and first-byte evidence.
